summary: Capability maps can become stale benchmark catalogs that add routing complexity without predicting production outcomes.

points.text: Provider updates, hidden system prompts, quantization, regional infrastructure, and tool changes can alter behavior without changing a public model name, invalidating old evaluations.
Task labels are often assigned from the same ambiguous user input the model must solve. Misclassification can route a hard or sensitive case to a cheap model with no chance to recover.
A router adds latency, cost, another model dependency, and new privacy exposure. For a narrow workload, one well-tested model plus deterministic fallbacks may be simpler and safer.
Benchmark optimization can hide rare but severe failures. Average quality and cost improvements do not establish acceptability for irreversible, regulated, or adversarial cases.
